packages.title: England drought 3 percent LTA rainfall QA
facts: Environment Agency reports only 3% of long-term-average rainfall for the latest July reporting period.
The figure is a hydrological condition indicator rather than a GHG emission.
Rainfall context can affect agriculture and water demand.
It must not be converted to emissions without a separate causal model.
No parcel CO2e value is inferred.

packages.title: England drought 84 percent river flows below normal QA
facts: Environment Agency reports 84% of river flows were classified below normal or lower.
Flow classification is a water-resource indicator.
It does not directly measure energy use or GHG emissions.
Hydrological status should remain separate from emissions accounting.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: England reservoir storage 75.3 percent QA
facts: England reservoir storage fell to 75.3% in the week ending 21 July 2026.
Environment Agency reports this was 7.4% below the long-term average for the time of year.
Reservoir storage is a capacity indicator rather than an emissions quantity.
Operating rules can differ among reservoirs.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from storage level.

packages.title: England water restrictions population share QA
facts: Environment Agency reports almost 40% of England's population faced water-use restrictions in the latest drought update.
Temporary use bans are water-demand management measures.
Restriction coverage is not a GHG metric.
Population exposure should not be substituted for emissions.
No parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: England 1,353 abstraction restrictions QA
facts: The drought update reports 1,353 abstraction licence restrictions linked to low river flows.
An abstraction restriction is a regulatory water-resource status.
Restriction counts are not emissions measurements.
Agricultural impacts can require separate activity evidence before emissions implications are assessed.
No parcel GHG value is inferred.

packages.title: England 61 drought incidents QA
facts: Environment Agency reports 61 confirmed drought and dry-weather incidents since the start of 2026.
The report also identifies algae and dead-fish incidents attributed to drought conditions.
Environmental-incident counts are not greenhouse-gas totals.
Incident attribution can be incomplete or underestimated.
No parcel emissions are inferred from incident counts.

packages.title: UK 119,080 public EV chargers QA
facts: DfT reports 119,080 public EV chargers in the UK as of 1 April 2026.
The statistic measures charging infrastructure stock.
Charger count is not electricity consumption.
Infrastructure stock is also not a GHG emission amount.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from charger count.

packages.title: UK 27,372 rapid-or-above chargers QA
facts: DfT reports 27,372 public EV chargers rated rapid or above at 50 kW+ as of 1 April 2026.
Power rating is infrastructure capability rather than actual energy delivered.
A rated charger can have different utilization over time.
Charger power must not be converted directly to emissions without usage and electricity-factor data.
No parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: EV charger versus device methodology change QA
facts: From 2026 the DfT statistical series focuses on public EV chargers rather than the earlier charging-device measure.
ONS notes the change better represents the number of vehicles that can be charged.
The definition change creates a comparability break with earlier device-count series.
Historic device counts should not be compared mechanically with current charger counts.
Neither measure is a GHG emission value.

packages.title: July 2026 monthly EV charger indicator QA
facts: DfT updated monthly public EV charger indicators to include 1 July 2026 data.
The monthly indicator is more frequent than the quarterly infrastructure release.
Monthly and quarterly publications can have different reference dates and methods.
The indicator is infrastructure stock rather than emissions.
No parcel emissions are inferred.

packages.title: 1 July EV quarterly release future guard QA
facts: The quarterly EV charging infrastructure publication for 1 July 2026 is scheduled for August 2026.
As of 25 July 2026 the quarterly release is not yet an observed published dataset.
Available July monthly indicators must not be relabelled as the future quarterly release.
Future values are not fabricated.
QA preserves the release-status distinction.

packages.title: Q1 2026 769,000 first vehicle registrations QA
facts: DfT reports 769,000 vehicles were registered for the first time in the UK in January to March 2026.
This was 5.1% higher than the same quarter of 2025.
First registrations are a flow measure.
Registration flow is distinct from the licensed vehicle stock.
Vehicle counts are not direct GHG emissions.

packages.title: Q1 2026 150,000 ZEV first registrations QA
facts: DfT reports 150,000 zero-emission vehicles were registered for the first time in Q1 2026.
The flow was 12.9% higher than Q1 2025.
DfT's ZEV definition is based on reported zero grams CO2 per kilometre from the tailpipe.
Tailpipe-zero does not by itself represent lifecycle-zero emissions.
No parcel GHG value is inferred from registration counts.

packages.title: Heat-pump deployment up to 45 kW scope QA
facts: DESNZ heat-pump deployment statistics cover hydronic heat pumps with capacity up to 45 kW.
The statistics monitor installation counts in the UK.
Installation count and rated capacity are not measured heat output.
They are also not direct GHG savings.
No parcel emissions reduction is inferred from installation status alone.

packages.title: Heat-pump statistics provisional development QA
facts: DESNZ labels the heat-pump deployment series as official statistics in development.
The series is provisional and subject to future revisions.
Quarterly counts are used to monitor deployment.
Revision status must be preserved in downstream QA.
No parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Boiler Upgrade Scheme May 2026 workflow QA
facts: The May 2026 Boiler Upgrade Scheme statistics report scheme uptake using applications and voucher redemptions.
They also include installation cost information.
Application, voucher issuance and redemption are different workflow states.
The June 2026 BUS release is scheduled for 30 July 2026 and is not yet current as of 25 July.
Scheme workflow counts are not measured parcel GHG reductions.

packages.title: SHDF two-month reporting lag QA
facts: The June 2026 Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund release covers measures installed and households upgraded in England.
Monthly data are reported two months in arrears.
The figures are provisional and subject to revision.
Measure installation counts are not direct emissions measurements.
No dwelling-level GHG reduction is inferred without separate evidence.

packages.title: Warm Homes Social Housing Fund under-reporting QA
facts: The June 2026 WH:SHF release was based on returns from 41 of 138 participating grant recipients.
It reported around 4,850 measures in around 2,600 households through the reporting period.
DESNZ states current figures likely significantly under-report actual activity.
Provisional scheme delivery data should not be treated as complete stock coverage.
No parcel emissions reduction is inferred.

packages.title: 2024/25 local-authority waste final activity guard QA
facts: Defra's 2024/25 local-authority collected waste results are final annual activity statistics for England.
The release reports waste generation, recycling and treatment-management measures.
Waste tonnes and recycling rates are activity indicators rather than direct GHG emissions.
Waste-emissions estimates require separate inventory methods and boundaries.
No parcel CO2e is inferred from waste activity alone.

packages.title: 2025 road traffic activity versus GHG guard QA
facts: DfT reports 2025 car traffic at 262.4 billion vehicle miles and van traffic at 58.8 billion vehicle miles in Great Britain.
Lorry traffic was 16.3 billion vehicle miles.
England's Strategic Road Network carried 99.2 billion vehicle miles.
Vehicle miles are transport activity measures, not direct GHG emissions.
No parcel road-transport emission is inferred without compatible fleet, fuel and spatial allocation evidence.
